newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Chinese explore new trade, investment in Zimbabwe.
newsitem.headline: Chinese explore new trade, investment in Zimbabwe.

text.p: A Chinese business delegation arrived in Zimbabwe on Wednesday to explore new trade and investment opportunities.
Its visit follows the signing in May of several trade pacts between Harare and Beijing during a state visit to the southern African state by Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
The 22-member delegation met officials from the Zimbabwe National Chamber of Commerce (ZNCC) to discuss prospects of trade and joint business ventures.
ZNCC president Danny Meyer said the May agreements had demonstrated a willingness by the two governments to broaden trade relations.
"This sent clear signals to the business community and we would like to see rapid acceleration in the level of trade between China and Zimbabwe," Meyer said, adding:
"It is not just in the field of trade that we expect growth but also in the level of investment through joint ventures and licensing agreements".
Latest available figures show that trade between the two countries rose to Z$810 million in 1994 from Z$580 million the previous year.
Vice-President Simon Muzenda is expected to lead a Zimbabwean business delegation to China on November 6 to boost trade relations between the two countries.
